# ARIA

> ARIA does the first pass of incident triage. It reads an alert or a burst of log lines, rates severity with rules, a calibrated model and a conformal prediction set, and finds the most similar past incidents. The prediction set promises coverage for each severity level, tighter for SEV1 and SEV2, and certifies a limit on how often a serious incident is rated minor; a novelty check sends windows unlike anything the model learned from, and systems it never trained on, to a person. ARIA then drafts an incident report in which every claim cites evidence, and waits for a human to approve it; every decision goes on an append-only, hash-chained record. It is open source (MIT), runs offline with no keys, and can use Google Gemini (one key serves a pool of models, each kept inside its own limits), NVIDIA NIM, Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI or any OpenAI-compatible model.

Results are measured in three rings: fresh windows of the systems the model learned from; systems and failure modes it never saw, each held out in turn with the model refitted without it; and real data with the labels its owners gave it: a Hadoop cluster's log, replayed window by window against the label Hadoop experts gave every storage block; the whole BlueGene/L log, in windows labelled by its administrators' alert tags; Hadoop jobs with injected failures; OpenStack runs with injected bugs; failed CI builds; a ServiceNow service desk's tickets; GitLab.com's production incidents, with its responders' labels; three clouds' post-mortems; public prompt-injection benchmarks; and data from fields ARIA was never tuned on (security alerts from attacked networks, faults injected into microservice shops, Kubernetes incidents and public Jira priorities). A registry records what each suite was tuned on. The other results come from semi-synthetic incidents (real Loghub log lines composed into incidents) and are not accuracy on production incidents. Blind checks, a person rating an incident before seeing ARIA's level, recalibrate the prediction sets, and a drift monitor watches each system's mix of levels. The API is REST with server-sent events. ARIA also speaks MCP (read-only tools), A2A (an agent card plus JSON-RPC tasks) and AG-UI.

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ManavParmar1609/ARIA/main/README.md): what ARIA does, quickstart, provider setup including Gemini and NVIDIA NIM, how severity is decided, safety controls, test results, limitations
- [Agent skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ManavParmar1609/ARIA/main/skills/aria-triage/SKILL.md): how an agent starts a triage run, reads the cited report and hands it to a human for review
- [Evaluation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ManavParmar1609/ARIA/main/docs/evaluation.md): every measured number, its data and its method, by ring
- [Model card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ManavParmar1609/ARIA/main/docs/model-card.md): the severity model, its per-level calibration and conformal sets, the novelty check, recalibration on blind checks, drift, and the third-party models ARIA calls
- [Data card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ManavParmar1609/ARIA/main/docs/data-card.md): datasets, licences, the real labelled logs, and how the semi-synthetic incidents and labels are built
- [Threat model](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ManavParmar1609/ARIA/main/docs/threat-model.md): trust boundaries, prompt injection, the red team and the controls that handle it

## API

- [OpenAPI schema](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ManavParmar1609/ARIA/main/docs/openapi.json): runs, event stream, reports, review, history and forks, alert webhooks, Ask ARIA, incidents, runbooks, real incidents to replay, feedback and blind checks, drift, the decision record, model capacity, evaluation

## Optional

- [Architecture decisions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ManavParmar1609/ARIA/main/docs/adr/README.md): why one LangGraph graph, the severity cascade, grounded reports, per-level coverage promises, three rings of tests, the model pool, the decision record and the rest
- [Validation log](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ManavParmar1609/ARIA/main/docs/validation-log.md): every candidate change to the severity rules and thresholds, chosen on validation seeds only, adopted or not
- [The EU AI Act](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ManavParmar1609/ARIA/main/docs/eu-ai-act.md): why ARIA, as shipped, is not a high-risk system, and what would change that
- [Ops runbook](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ManavParmar1609/ARIA/main/docs/ops-runbook.md): deploying, configuring, monitoring and troubleshooting ARIA, including recalibration, the severe-miss alarm, retention and the decision record
- [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ManavParmar1609/ARIA/main/AGENTS.md): conventions for coding agents working on the repository
- [Build brief](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ManavParmar1609/ARIA/main/docs/build-brief.md): the specification and its acceptance checks
